mola_megdr_16ppd.title: MGS MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record (MEGDR), 16 pixel/degree global topography (MEGT90N000EB)
mola_megdr_16ppd.institution: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / Goddard Space Flight Center (MOLA Science Team)
mola_megdr_16ppd.instrument_or_model: Mars Global Surveyor / Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA)
mola_megdr_16ppd.coverage: Global, 90N-90S, 0-360E; simple cylindrical; IAU2000; areoid GMM3 (mgm1025) to degree and order 50
mola_megdr_16ppd.spatial_resolution: 0.0625 deg (16 ppd) = ~3.7 km per cell at the equator
mola_megdr_16ppd.observation_period: 1997-09-15 to 2001-06-30 (MGS mapping, primary and extended missions)
mola_megdr_16ppd.uncertainty_notes: Each cell is the MEDIAN of MOLA shots inside it; near the equator only ~55% of cells contain a shot and the rest are interpolated, with gaps of up to 12 km between profiles. Individual shot vertical accuracy is ~1 m; interpolated cells inherit the local relief uncertainty. Slopes and roughness are REGIONAL (~3.7 km baseline) and say nothing about metre-scale hazards.
mola_megdr_16ppd.access_method: HTTPS download of the raw binary + PDS3 label (scripts/fetch_mola.py)
mola_megdr_16ppd.license: NASA PDS data are public domain; cite the MOLA Science Team

derived_toa_insolation.title: Top-of-atmosphere annual-mean insolation from latitude and orbital elements
derived_toa_insolation.instrument_or_model: Analytic daily-mean insolation integrated over one orbit (a=1.52368 AU, e=0.0934, obliquity 25.19 deg, Ls_perihelion 251 deg, S0=1361 W/m2)
derived_toa_insolation.spatial_resolution: Latitude only; no terrain or atmosphere
derived_toa_insolation.uncertainty_notes: Model output, not a measurement. Ignores atmospheric dust opacity (which can cut surface flux by tens of percent) and local horizon. Use as a latitude-driven proxy only.

factor_scores.label: Terrain safety (regional slope)
factor_scores.rationale: Lower regional slopes reduce the chance that a landing ellipse spans tilted terrain such as crater walls or rises. The 2 deg 'fully suitable' knee echoes the km-scale slope constraint reported for Mars Exploration Rover site selection (Golombek et al., 2003, J. Geophys. Res. 108(E12), 8072); the 10 deg cut-off is an assumption for coarse screening. MEGDR 16 ppd slopes are regional (~3.7 km baseline) and cannot reveal lander-scale (metres) hazards.

factor_scores.label: Elevation suitability (EDL atmosphere)
factor_scores.rationale: Lower elevation means a thicker atmospheric column for entry, descent and landing deceleration. Historical engineering limits ranged from below -1.3 km (MER, Golombek et al. 2003) to around +1 km or lower for guided-entry missions (MSL, Mars 2020). The -3000 m / +2000 m knees are a screening assumption spanning that range; a real mission's limit depends on its EDL system.

factor_scores.label: Surface roughness (detrended relief)
factor_scores.rationale: Standard deviation of MOLA elevation within the footprint after removing a best-fit plane. Low values indicate smooth plains at the km scale; high values indicate crater rims, scarps or hummocky terrain. Knees are assumptions tuned so smooth plains score near 1 and crater-wall-dominated footprints score near 0. Not a proxy for rock abundance or decimetre-scale roughness.

factor_scores.label: Thermal conditions
factor_scores.excluded_reason: feature surface_temperature_mean_c missing on 8/8 sites; excluded for all under common_feature_set
factor_scores.rationale: Warmer mean surface temperatures ease thermal management for landed hardware. PLACEHOLDER: no Mars site carries this feature in profile v1 (THEMIS/TES integration is an open Engineer-2 task), so under the common_feature_set policy this criterion is excluded and reported in completeness rather than scored.

factor_scores.label: Solar illumination (annual mean, top of atmosphere)
factor_scores.rationale: Annual-mean top-of-atmosphere insolation computed from latitude and Mars orbital elements (see SCIENTIFIC_METHOD.md). Near-equatorial latitudes approach ~185 W/m2; the poles approach ~80 W/m2. Ignores atmospheric dust opacity and local horizon, so it is a latitude-driven proxy for solar power availability, not a surface measurement.

criteria.label: Elevation suitability (EDL atmosphere)
criteria.rationale: Lower elevation means a thicker atmospheric column for entry, descent and landing deceleration. Historical engineering limits ranged from below -1.3 km (MER, Golombek et al. 2003) to around +1 km or lower for guided-entry missions (MSL, Mars 2020). The -3000 m / +2000 m knees are a screening assumption spanning that range; a real mission's limit depends on its EDL system.

criteria.label: Surface roughness (detrended relief)
criteria.rationale: Standard deviation of MOLA elevation within the footprint after removing a best-fit plane. Low values indicate smooth plains at the km scale; high values indicate crater rims, scarps or hummocky terrain. Knees are assumptions tuned so smooth plains score near 1 and crater-wall-dominated footprints score near 0. Not a proxy for rock abundance or decimetre-scale roughness.

criteria.label: Thermal conditions
criteria.rationale: Warmer mean surface temperatures ease thermal management for landed hardware. PLACEHOLDER: no Mars site carries this feature in profile v1 (THEMIS/TES integration is an open Engineer-2 task), so under the common_feature_set policy this criterion is excluded and reported in completeness rather than scored.

criteria.label: Solar illumination (annual mean, top of atmosphere)
criteria.rationale: Annual-mean top-of-atmosphere insolation computed from latitude and Mars orbital elements (see SCIENTIFIC_METHOD.md). Near-equatorial latitudes approach ~185 W/m2; the poles approach ~80 W/m2. Ignores atmospheric dust opacity and local horizon, so it is a latitude-driven proxy for solar power availability, not a surface measurement.

notes: Scores are relative decision-support indices on 0-100, not probabilities and not a landing-safety certification.
Every threshold below is a DOCUMENTED ASSUMPTION chosen for regional screening at the ~3.7 km MOLA MEGDR 16 ppd baseline. None is an established universal landing requirement.
Suitability functions are piecewise-linear: q = 1 at or beyond `full` toward the preferred direction, q = 0 at or beyond `zero`, linear in between.
